text: Went to Rosalind's Diner on Fenwick Ave last night and wow, it has gone downhill. Waited 50 min for cold eggs, the server rolled her eyes when we asked for the check, and the booth was sticky. Used to be our Sunday spot. Never again.
why: Harsh criticism of a business's service is explicitly allowed.

text: Councilmember Darla Pruitt voted to cut Saturday library hours AGAIN. That's shortsighted and honestly embarrassing for a district with this many kids. Call her office and tell her what you think before the Nov 12 meeting.
why: Criticism of a public official's decisions and urging civic contact is allowed.

text: The leaf blower ban idea is ridiculous. Half of us are older and can't rake an acre by hand. Whoever drafted this clearly doesn't own a yard.
why: Harsh disagreement with a proposal, not an attack on a specific person.

text: PSA: Brightline Plumbing charged us $480 to 'fix' a leak that started again two days later, then wouldn't return calls. Save yourself the headache.
why: A negative review of a business's service is allowed.

text: The new HOA rule about trash cans being out of sight by 8am is absurd. Some of us work nights. Board needs to rethink this.
why: Criticism of a policy, not a person.

text: Gary Mendel on Birchwood Ct is the laziest, dumbest excuse for a human I've ever met. His yard is a dump and so is he.
why: Insults aimed at a specific named private person.

text: that [slur] who moved into the yellow duplex on Pike st needs to learn how things work around here
why: Slur aimed at an identifiable person.

text: Has anyone seen the lady who walks the three poodles on Grove? She dresses like a clown lol. Somebody get a pic next time 😂😂
why: Mockery of an identifiable person, plus encouraging others to target her.

text: Everyone please flood Tina Okafor's inbox and let her know what we think of her complaining to the city about our block party. Make her regret it.
why: Encourages others to target a specific person.

text: Megan I have messaged you 14 times and you keep ignoring me. I'm going to keep posting here every day until you answer. You can't hide forever.
why: Repeated unwanted contact directed at a specific person.

text: The Hendricks kid on Lowell Rd who keeps skateboarding past my house is the most annoying little weirdo. Kid looks like a malnourished rat.
why: Mocking insults aimed at an identifiable minor.

text: If I see Derek Holm anywhere near my driveway again I am going to beat him senseless. Consider this his warning.
why: A conditional threat of violence against a named person.

text: Somebody should teach the guy in unit 4B a lesson he won't walk away from. I know what time he gets home and where he parks.
why: An implied violent threat combined with knowledge of the target's schedule.

text: Ray at the corner store on 9th better watch his back. I'm done talking. He'll find out soon enough.
why: A threat of harm against an identifiable person.

text: My ex Jordan thinks they can move three streets over and I won't notice. If they show up at the farmers market Saturday they won't be leaving in one piece.
why: A conditional threat of violence against a specific person.

text: The people at 410 who called animal control on my dog better hope their house doesn't catch fire some night. Just saying.
why: A veiled threat of arson against identifiable people.

text: Huge thank you to whoever in the blue house on Larkspur keeps letting their dog do its business on my lawn every morning. Truly a pillar of the community 👏
why: Sarcastic complaint about behavior that is likely to start conflict, but it criticizes conduct and contains no insult, so it falls short of removable mockery.

text: I swear I could kill my neighbor's rooster. 4:45am EVERY DAY. Does anyone know the city rules on roosters?
why: A common figure of speech about an animal followed by a genuine question, not a threat against a person.

text: To the guy in the white pickup who blocks my hydrant every Thursday: do it one more time and you'll regret it. I'm not calling the tow truck next time.
why: 'Not calling the tow truck' turns a vague warning into an implied conditional threat of personal action against an identifiable driver.

text: Phil who owns Kessler Hardware is a crook. Charged me for a full gallon of stain, gave me a quart, and called me a liar when I showed him the receipt. Shop elsewhere.
why: Although it names the owner, 'crook' is tied to a specific service complaint about how the business is run.

text: Mayor Tom Bracken's comb-over must be blocking his view of all the potholes on Ridge Rd lol
why: Officials can be criticized for decisions, but this mocks his appearance, which counts as mockery of an identifiable person.

text: Commissioner Ellis is an absolute clown for pushing the Westgate rezoning through without a single public hearing. He should resign.
why: Harsh name-calling, but it is tied directly to a public official's decision.

text: Third time posting: Jen from the PTA, PLEASE return my blue casserole dish from the potluck 😅 It was my grandma's!
why: Repeated, but friendly and good-natured rather than harassing or unwanted in a hostile way.

text: Someone spray painted [slur] on the fence by the Corbin Park playground overnight. Disgusting. City has been called and they're sending a crew. Please keep an eye out.
why: It reports hateful vandalism rather than aiming a slur at anyone (and the slur is already redacted).

text: We should all go stand outside Barry's house on Sunday afternoon so he knows exactly how the street feels about that 8 foot fence. Strength in numbers.
why: Organizing a group to gather at a private person's home is encouraging others to target him, even without an explicit threat.

text: @Marco you absolute goblin, you STILL owe me a taco from the block party cornhole bet 😂🌮
why: Clearly friendly ribbing between acquaintances, not a genuine insult.

text: People who don't pick up after their dogs on the greenway are trash. Simple as that.
why: A harsh generalization about a behavior, not aimed at any identifiable person.

text: Whoever stole three packages off my porch Tuesday, I hope you get hit by a bus.
why: Wishing harm on an unknown person is not a threat by the poster, but it is hostile and likely to cause conflict.

text: Do NOT hire Kaylee Brandt for babysitting. She was on her phone the entire time and we came home to our toddler alone in the backyard.
why: Names a private person, but it is a factual review of a paid service that matters for safety, with no insults.

text: To whoever keeps emptying the Little Free Library on Ashby: we have a camera now. Enjoy your upcoming fame 📸
why: A deterrent warning to an unknown person that implies exposure, not violence.

text: Anybody who comes up on my porch uninvited after dark is getting a face full of 12-gauge. Just saying, with all these break-ins.
why: Even though it is framed as self-defense and has no named target, it is a conditional threat of gun violence against people.

text: Karen on Delmont strikes again 🙄 called the cops on the kids' lemonade stand. Some people need a hobby.
why: Mocks an identifiable neighbor by street and incident, whether 'Karen' is her real name or an insult.

text: To my neighbor at 22 Oriole Ln: blasting music at 2am on a weeknight is inconsiderate. Please stop. Some of us have jobs.
why: It falls under privacy as well as harassment: it posts a private person's address, and the mild frustration probably falls short of the hostility needed for escalation.

text: Landlord Victor Szabo is a slumlord. My unit has had black mold for six months and he won't return a single call. Tenants on Crane St, document everything.
why: Harsh criticism of a landlord's business conduct with specific complaints.

text: Oh great, Dennis is running for HOA board again. Can't wait for another year of him 'forgetting' to post the budget 🙃
why: Sarcasm about a candidate's record is fair criticism, but its personal tone toward a neighbor is likely to cause conflict.

text: Some people on this app really need to get a life. You know who you are.
why: A vague subtweet with no identifiable target, but likely to stir conflict.

text: "I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse" — me, to whoever keeps getting the last shady parking spot at Glenmoor Park lol
why: A joking movie quote with no real threat intended.

text: The weird guy who mutters to himself at the bus stop on Hale St every morning is creepy. Someone should do something about him.
why: Mocks an identifiable, possibly vulnerable person and vaguely encourages others to act against him, though it stops short of a clear threat.

text: If the city doesn't put a light at Orchard & 5th, somebody is going to get killed. Third near-miss with a kid this month.
why: Sounds alarming but is a safety prediction aimed at a public service, not a threat.

text: Sarah, I know you blocked me everywhere but I just want to apologize in person. Please DM me or I'll keep trying. I'm not giving up on us.
why: A sincere-sounding apology, but it gets around a block to keep contacting someone who doesn't want it, which is repeated unwanted contact.

text: Beautiful 2BR apt on Hollis Ave, $650/mo with all utilities included!! I'm overseas on mission work right now so I can't show it, but if you wire the $1,300 deposit + first month to my agent I'll FedEx the keys same day. Serious inquiries only, God bless.
why: This is a textbook fake rental: the price is far too low, the owner is away so nobody can see the unit, and the deposit has to be wired before anyone gets keys.

text: PS5 disc edition w/ 2 controllers $200. Payment ONLY in Steam or Google Play gift cards, send me the codes and I'll ship tomorrow. No cash sorry
why: The post asks to be paid in gift cards, which the policy names as a scam.

text: 🎉 CONGRATULATIONS Corkboard neighbors! 🎉 Your household has been selected for a $500 Brightline Grocers voucher for being a loyal shopper. Claim within 24 hrs by entering your name, SSN and bank login at the form in my profile!!
why: It's a fake prize set up to collect Social Security numbers and bank logins.

text: HIRING work-from-home envelope stuffers, earn $800/wk!! No experience. Just pay the $75 starter kit fee to my CashApp and I'll mail your first batch.
why: It's an advance-fee job scam: you pay money first for work that almost certainly doesn't exist.

text: NOTICE FROM MARLOW COUNTY WATER DEPT: Several Fernwood accounts are 60 days past due. To avoid shutoff TODAY call 555-0192 and pay with prepaid gift cards. This is your final warning.
why: The post pretends to be a government utility and demands gift-card payment, which breaks both the scam rule and the impersonation rule.

text: Selling my 2014 Corolla, 98k miles, new tires last spring, small dent rear bumper. $7,800 obo. Can meet at the Pine St police station lot for test drive. Have title in hand.
why: This is an ordinary sale with real details, a safe meeting spot and the title on hand.

text: Graco crib + mattress, $40. Smoke free home. Porch pickup on Larkspur Ct, cash or Venmo when you get here.
why: This is a plain buy/sell post where you pay when you pick it up.

text: 1962 Halvorsen hollowbody guitar, all original, case included. $4,500 FIRM. I know what I have, no lowballers please. Happy to let you play it at my place before you buy.
why: The price is high, but high prices are explicitly allowed and the seller offers to let buyers try it in person.

text: Heads up neighbors — got a call today from someone saying they were from Fernwood Savings and needed to 'verify' my debit card PIN. Bank says they never call for that. Don't give out your info!
why: A neighbor warning others about a scam call is useful and doesn't break any rule.

text: Is this text legit?? Says my package from 'Fernwood Post' is held and I need to pay a $1.99 redelivery fee at a link. I didn't order anything lol
why: The post is a question asking whether something is a scam, and questions are allowed.

text: Multi-family garage sale Sat 8-1 at 40 Birchwood Dr! Kids clothes, tools, kitchen stuff, a treadmill. Early birds welcome after 7:30.
why: This is an ordinary local sale announcement.

text: Renting out the downstairs unit at our duplex, 112 Quarry Rd. 1BR, $1,250, available Dec 1. Open house Sunday 2-4 — come see it, application after viewing. — Dana & Luis
why: This is a normal rental listing where people can see the unit before applying.

text: Yorkie puppies, AKC, $250 each!! Vet checked. I'm not able to do local pickup right now, shipping only through our pet transport partner. Text me on WhatsApp only, I don't check this app.
why: The red flags are very cheap purebred puppies, shipping only and contact moved off the app, so it looks suspicious even though fraud isn't proven.

text: brand new sealed iphone 17 pro max $300. dont have receipt. cash only, i'll come to you, no meeting at police station
why: The very low price, no receipt and refusal to meet somewhere safe make this suspicious, though it isn't clearly a scam.

text: 2 floor tix for Velvet Harbor at the Arena Fri, $180 for both. Zelle me and I'll send screenshots of the tickets right after.
why: Ticket screenshots sent after a Zelle payment is a common resale scam pattern, but nothing here clearly proves fraud.

text: To the guy on Dunmore St who sold me that 'working' snowblower — I know which house is yours. Refund my $400 by Friday or you're gonna regret it, I'm not playing.
why: Whatever happened with the sale, this is a conditional threat against a person, so the harassment rule calls for escalation.

text: Jordan 1 Retro 'Midnight Lake' size 10, DS. $900 firm. Yes I know retail was $180, that's not what they go for. DM only.
why: The price looks like gouging, but high prices on ordinary sales are explicitly allowed and nothing suggests a false offer.

text: Starting a Powerball pool for the Oak Hollow block! $20 a person, Venmo me by Wednesday and I'll post a pic of the tickets before the drawing. If we win we split evenly 🤞
why: A neighbor's lottery pool may be harmless, but collecting money from strangers on trust with nothing to check is hard to verify, so it's suspicious without being clearly fraudulent.

text: FREE sectional couch, great shape, just moving and don't want to haul it. I'll even deliver it! Only ask $30 for gas/delivery, send on CashApp first so I know you're serious.
why: Paying upfront to a stranger for a 'free' item is a common advance-fee pattern, but a small gas fee could be honest, so it's suspicious rather than clearly fraud.

text: Selling a $100 Brightline Grocers gift card for $85, got 2 for my birthday and only need one. Can meet at the store and you can check the balance at customer service before paying.
why: The post mentions gift cards, but the seller is selling one with an in-person balance check, not asking to be paid in gift cards.

text: Interested in anyone's riding lawnmower. My bank account is frozen rn so I'd pay with Apple gift cards, I can do $50 over asking to make up for the hassle.
why: This isn't a request to pay with gift cards, but a buyer offering gift cards plus extra money matches stolen-card and overpayment patterns, so it's suspicious but not clearly fraud.

text: I'll buy your patio set for $350. I'm relocating so my company will mail you a cashier's check for $1,200 — just Zelle the difference to my movers and they'll pick it up.
why: It looks like an ordinary buy offer, but the plan to overpay and have the seller send the difference is a known scam designed to take money under false pretenses.

text: Ridgeback Remodeling here (local, licensed #4471). For kitchen jobs we require a 40% deposit before we order materials — contract signed first, receipts for everything. Booking January now.
why: A deposit up front can look like an advance-fee scam, but this is a normal contractor practice with a license number, a contract and receipts.

text: So sad about the Petrakis family's house fire on Wren St 💔 I set up a fundraiser for them, link in comments, please give whatever you can! (I don't know them personally but I want to help)
why: It may be a kind gesture, but someone with no connection to the family collecting money for them can't be verified and fits a common fake-fundraiser pattern.

text: selling my brother in law, slightly used, eats a lot, will take 3 amazon gift cards or best offer 😂 (he's been on our couch since July send help)
why: It mentions gift-card payment, but it's an obvious joke and isn't a real offer meant to take anyone's money.

text: My cousin's crypto trading group has gotten me 30% returns since spring, no joke. Minimum buy-in is $1,000. DM me if you want me to add you, spots are limited.
why: Big claimed returns, a buy-in and 'limited spots' are investment-scam signals, but it could be a real personal experience, so it's suspicious rather than clearly fraud.

text: House for rent on Kestrel Ln, 3BR, $1,100. Landlord is strict so I can't do showings until your application is approved. $45 app fee via Zelle, I'll send you the form.
why: Application fees are normal, but paying before you can see the place and the low rent are fake-rental warning signs, though not conclusive.

text: Have 2 extra tix to the Marlow Mudcats home opener, paid $40 each, asking $75 each since it's sold out. Can transfer through the team app once you pay.
why: Reselling above face value is just a high price, and a transfer through the official app is a legitimate way to deliver the tickets.

text: Elm Park PTA raffle! $5 a ticket or 5 for $20 — prizes include a spa basket and a $200 Gino's gift card. Drawing at the Fall Fair Nov 9, you don't need to be present to win.
why: Prizes and gift cards can make this look like a fake-prize scam, but it's an ordinary school raffle with a public drawing.

text: Rosetti's Pizza giveaway!!! 🍕 SHARE this post and tag 3 neighbors to be entered to win a FREE large pizza every week for a year! The more you share the more entries!!
why: Even if the prize is real, 'share this to win' is engagement bait, which the spam rule removes, and that's stricter than the scam rule's LIMIT.

text: Rolex Submariner style watch — to be clear it's a REPLICA, not real, I'm not trying to fool anyone. $60. Keeps good time.
why: Fake designer goods look like fraud, but the seller clearly says it's a replica, so nobody is being misled.

text: Authentic Louis Vuitton Neverfull, 100% genuine, $80. Lost the receipt and dust bag. Price is low because I need it gone today.
why: Claiming a real luxury bag at a fraction of its price with no proof and pressure to buy today is suspicious, but the sale isn't clearly fraudulent.

text: Careful using the parking meters on Ash St — I scanned the QR sticker on one and it took me to a sketchy payment site that didn't look like the city's. Might be a fake sticker? Used the coin slot instead.
why: It's unconfirmed, but it's a neighbor's personal experience and a safety warning, not a misleading claim made to deceive.

text: Rehoming our cat Biscuit 😿 landlord won't allow pets. Spayed, chipped, all shots. $75 rehoming fee to make sure she goes to someone serious. Meet her first at our place on Garnet Ave.
why: A rehoming fee can look like a pet scam, but it's a common practice here and buyers can meet the cat in person first.

text: Re: the lost golden retriever on Maple — I think I have your dog. I'm about 40 min out so send $100 on Venmo for gas first and I'll bring him tonight. Can't send a photo, phone camera is broken.
why: It's framed as a lost-and-found reply, but demanding money first while refusing any proof is an advance-fee scam aimed at a desperate owner.

text: Selling sealed Xbox Series X, $250. I'm currently deployed so my shipping agent handles all sales. PayPal Friends & Family only so there are no fees for either of us 🇺🇸
why: The low price, the 'deployed with a shipping agent' story and a payment method with no buyer protection make this a known scam script, not just a suspicious listing.

text: Taking preorders for holiday cookie boxes! 🎄 $35/box, a dozen assorted. Venmo to reserve, pickup Dec 20 from my porch on Sycamore. I did this last year too, check the comments for reviews!
why: Paying ahead looks like an advance-fee scam, but it's a normal preorder from a local seller with a pickup date and past reviews.

text: MOVING TOMORROW must sell 2019 Honda Civic $2,000!! runs great. cash only. title is with my mom in another state but I'll mail it to you after
why: A cheap car with no title on hand and a rush to sell are strong red flags, but a real move could explain it, so it's suspicious rather than clearly fraud.

text: Hi! I'm collecting donations for Veterans of Marlow this weekend, going door to door on Fenwick & Crane. Cash only, we're still waiting on our nonprofit paperwork so no receipts yet. Thank you for supporting our heroes!
why: An unregistered charity that takes cash only with no receipts is suspicious, but the collector could be sincere, so it isn't clearly fraudulent.

text: Selling my homemade cinnamon-bitter melon tea, $15/bag. It's helped my blood sugar so much I've cut way back on my metformin! Message me to order.
why: The sale itself is ordinary, but cutting back medication is presented as a personal story rather than advice to stop, so it sits just short of REMOVE under the misinformation rule and is hidden as misleading.

text: PSA for parents in Ridgeview: STOP giving your kids those steroid inhalers. The steroids are what's CAUSING the attacks, they weaken the lungs over time. We took my son off his in August and switched to eucalyptus steam at night. Do your own research but please don't keep poisoning your babies.
why: It tells parents to stop prescribed asthma medicine for children, a false health claim that could lead to physical harm.

text: cleaning hack my aunt taught me — mix bleach and ammonia 50/50 in a spray bottle, cuts through bathroom mold like nothing else. totally safe if you crack a window
why: It presents a mix that produces toxic gas as safe, which could directly cause physical harm.

text: For those of you without power on Kessler Rd: you can run your generator in the garage as long as you leave the big door open a foot or so. Carbon monoxide thing is way overblown, we've done it every storm.
why: It falsely says running a generator in a garage is safe, which can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

text: Type 2 here. My naturopath in Elm Hollow got me off insulin completely with cinnamon capsules and a bitter melon tea. If you're diabetic you don't need to be a slave to big pharma. Ditch the needles and DM me for the brand.
why: It urges diabetics to stop prescribed insulin, a false health claim that could cause serious harm.

text: If you smell gas near Maple & 3rd don't bother calling 911 or the gas company, it's just the line test they're doing all week. Just ignore it, its harmless.
why: Telling people to ignore a gas smell and not report it is a false safety claim that could lead to injury.

text: FYI street sweeping is done for the year in Lower Ashgrove, the city cancelled the rest of the schedule. No need to move your cars Tuesdays anymore!
why: It's a misleading claim about a city service that could get people ticketed but won't put anyone in physical danger.

text: Don't wait for the 14 bus at the Halvorsen stop anymore, they cut that route back in September. Walk to the 22 instead.
why: It's a misleading claim about public transit that inconveniences people but isn't dangerous.

text: Heads up — city just changed trick-or-treat hours to 4–6pm ONLY this year and police will be writing tickets to anyone out after 6. Spread the word!!
why: It's a made-up claim about a local event and police enforcement that causes confusion but not physical harm.

text: Pinecrest Farmers Market is closed for good, the vendors all pulled out over the new fees. Don't bother going Saturday.
why: It's a false-sounding, unverified claim about a local event that misleads people without putting anyone in danger.

text: Ignore what the parks dept website says, the Harvest Lantern Walk at Doyle Park is cancelled. My neighbor's cousin works there.
why: It contradicts the official event info with secondhand hearsay, which is misleading but not dangerous.

text: Honest question, not trying to start a fight — is it true the flu shot can give you the flu? My mom swears it does. Planning to take the kids to the Pine St clinic this weekend and want to know what to expect.
why: It's a sincere health question, and questions are explicitly allowed.

text: Went to Willow Wellness for acupuncture for my lower back after months of nothing working. 4 sessions in and I'm sleeping through the night. Not saying it's magic, ymmv, but it helped me.
why: It's a personal experience with a hedged recommendation and doesn't tell anyone to skip treatment.

text: Mark my words, that new roundabout at Cedar & 5th is going to cause more fender benders than the old 4-way stop ever did. Nobody around here knows how to yield.
why: It's a prediction and opinion about local infrastructure.

text: I think the city is throwing away money on the new water treatment plant when they could just upgrade the old one. $40 million?? Come on.
why: It's an opinion criticizing a public spending decision.

text: My daughter ran a fever for about 2 days after her 4-year shots. Pediatrician at Brookside said totally normal. Just sharing in case any other parents are worried this week.
why: It's an accurate personal experience shared to reassure other parents.

text: Does anyone know if the fireworks over Lake Tamsin are still happening Saturday with all the wind? Can't find anything on the town page.
why: It's a plain question about a local event.

text: Honestly I stopped taking my statin about 6 months ago and I feel better than I have in years. No more leg cramps. Just saying.
why: It's a personal experience that doesn't tell anyone else to stop their medication, though a reviewer might read it as implied encouragement.

text: Stopped my statins 6 months ago and my cholesterol is FINE, the whole cholesterol thing is a myth pushed by drug companies. Seriously if you're on them, try going off for a month and see how you feel.
why: It moves past personal experience into telling readers to stop prescribed medicine, which crosses the harm line.

text: Oh sure, go ahead and run the generator in the garage like the guy two streets over, what could possibly go wrong 🙄 Seriously people, OUTSIDE, 20 ft from the house.
why: It mentions a dangerous practice, but sarcastically, to warn people against it, and it gives correct safety advice.

text: Old family remedy that still works: a spoonful of raw honey for baby's cough. Worked on all 3 of mine, way better than the pharmacy stuff.
why: It's framed as personal experience, but it recommends honey for babies, which can cause infant botulism, so it promotes a dangerous practice as safe.

text: We've been getting raw milk from Hollow Creek Farm for 3 years and honestly it's so much better than store milk. Kids love it, tastes like actual milk.
why: Raw milk carries health risks, but this is a personal preference and experience without claiming it's safe for everyone.

text: The algae warning signs at Merrow Beach are overblown. We swam there all weekend with the dogs and everyone's fine. County just wants to cover themselves.
why: It uses personal experience to tell people an official toxic-algae warning is safe to ignore, which could lead to physical harm.

text: Found a bunch of what I think are false morels behind the Ransom trailhead. Is it true they're fine to eat if you boil them twice and dump the water? My grandpa always said so.
why: It repeats a dangerous belief, but as a sincere question, and questions are allowed.

text: Heard from someone who works at city hall that water rates are DOUBLING in January. Nobody's talking about it. Get ready.
why: It's an unverified rumor stated as fact about a public service, which misleads but isn't dangerous, though some reviewers might call it a harmless prediction.

text: The boil water advisory is only for the north side of Route 9. We're on Birch Lane, we're fine, been drinking tap all day.
why: If the advisory covers Birch Lane, this false safety claim could lead neighbors to drink contaminated water, though a reviewer without the advisory map might only LIMIT.

text: Pretty sure the Ashby Street clinic stopped taking Medicaid as of this month, so don't waste your time going there.
why: It's an uncertain but discouraging claim about a public health service that could mislead people, though the hedging makes it close to an allowed personal belief.

text: The fluoride in our town water is lowering our kids' IQ. There's studies. We switched to a filter pitcher and I'd recommend everyone do the same.
why: It's a contested health claim, but the advice (filtering water) poses no physical danger, so it falls under opinion rather than harmful misinformation.

text: Before you sign your kids up for the vaccine clinic at Linwood Elementary Thursday — please, please do your research. Vaccines and autism are linked, they just won't admit it. Protect your kids.
why: It doesn't say outright to skip vaccines, but it uses a false health claim to steer parents away from a specific clinic, which could lead to physical harm.

text: BREAKING: City Council votes 5-0 to declare the Juniper Ave potholes a protected historic landmark. Repairs now illegal. Tourism expected to boom. 🚧😂
why: It's formatted like a false news claim about a public service, but it's obvious satire and harmless.

text: Thanksgiving pro tip: deep fry the turkey frozen, in the garage, right next to the gas can. Extra crunchy and you get a free visit from the fire dept 😂🔥
why: It describes a dangerous practice, but the joke is plainly exaggerated and actually works as a warning, though a cautious reviewer could worry someone takes it literally.

text: Selling colloidal silver drops, $25/bottle, made locally. My family has used it instead of antibiotics for 4 years — ear infections, strep, all of it. Porch pickup on Wexford.
why: It looks like an ordinary for-sale post, but it pitches the product as a replacement for antibiotics, a false health claim that could cause harm.

text: Dr. Raman at Oakview Pediatrics is poisoning our kids with these shots and nobody is stopping him. Someone needs to deal with him before more kids get hurt.
why: It combines health misinformation with encouraging others to target a specific person, and 'deal with him' is vague enough that some reviewers would ESCALATE it as a veiled threat.
rekey_reason: Calls on others to "deal with" a doctor named at his workplace while accusing him of harming children; a location plus a call to confront.

text: Just so everyone knows, the family at 88 Larkspur Ct has measles and they REFUSE to vaccinate. Selfish people. Keep your kids far away from that house and let them know how you feel.
why: Beyond the health claim, it shares a private family's home address with hostility and encourages people to confront them, which meets the privacy escalation rule.

text: Oak St bridge is basically open again, the barricades are just leftover. I've driven over it twice this week, just go around the cones.
why: It's a claim about local roads, normally a LIMIT, but telling people to drive around barricades on a closed bridge is a dangerous safety claim.

text: Sirens going off right now are just the monthly test, don't panic everyone.
why: Without context it could be harmless, but if it isn't the scheduled test day, telling people to ignore warning sirens could lead to physical harm.

text: Calling it now: the Fallow Creek dam upstream is going to fail this winter. The county has ignored it for a decade.
why: It's alarming, but it's a prediction and criticism of the county, which the policy allows, though some reviewers might LIMIT it as fear-mongering.

text: CHECK YOUR KIDS' CANDY!! Someone in the Pinecrest neighborhood found needles in a Snickers last Halloween. Could happen again this year.
why: It's an unverified scare claim about a local event that misleads and alarms people without putting them in danger, though it could also be read as a cautious warning.

text: Diffusing tea tree oil around the house is a totally safe natural way to keep fleas off your cats. Way better than those chemical drops the vet pushes.
why: It falsely calls a practice that's toxic to cats safe; the harm is to pets rather than people, but it's still a dangerous safety claim.

text: Started a gaming channel!! would mean a lot if you guys subbed 🙏 youtube.com/@BirchwoodBenPlays
why: It's a resident's own content, but the YouTube channel isn't a local business or service, so it's low-value outside promotion rather than outright spam.

text: Anyone else been to Fenwick's Diner lately? Honestly the best breakfast in town, the new chef is incredible. (Reviewer note: the poster's account is linked to Fenwick's owner, who already posted a promo on Tuesday.)
why: Dressing up a second promotion in the same week as a neutral review is repetitive self-promotion, though one post isn't serious enough to remove.

text: Ugh, Summit Peak Roofing has posted their ad in this group like 6 times now. Anyone else getting annoyed? Please stop guys.
why: This is harsh criticism of a business's behavior, which is allowed, and it isn't spam itself.

text: Our school PTA raffle is on! Tickets $5 at the front office, prizes include a kayak. Share this post for an EXTRA ENTRY! 🛶
why: It's a legitimate local fundraiser, but giving extra prize entries for shares is "share to win" engagement bait.

text: PTA raffle tickets on sale at Whitcombe Elementary front office, $5 each, drawing Nov 15. Feel free to pass this along to grandparents!
why: Asking people to pass along a local fundraiser without rewarding shares with prizes is not engagement bait.

text: The Taco Loco truck will be parked outside Ashby Community Center every Thursday 5-8pm! We're based in Harlow City but love this neighborhood 🌮
why: The truck's home base is outside the area, but it operates in the neighborhood every week, so it works as a local business here.

text: Hi all, I'm the manager at Corbin Rd Hardware (I live in Harlow City but work here every day). We've got snow blowers in stock this week.
why: The business is in the neighborhood and this is a single weekly promotion, though the poster's address outside the area makes this a judgment call.

text: Hearthside Plumbing — we're on the Kessler Ave side, just past the neighborhood line by the gas station. 10% off for Maple Terrace folks!
why: A business just across the border that is clearly aimed at serving this neighborhood is effectively local, though a strict reviewer might LIMIT it.

text: Huge savings at local stores!! I found all the best Maple Terrace coupons here 👉 dealzhub-coupons.click/maple
why: The link is presented as local, but it goes to a generic outside coupon/affiliate site unrelated to any neighborhood business.

text: Win a FREE furnace tune-up from Okafor Heating! Just click the link and enter your card number to verify you're a local resident. Hurry, ends tonight!
why: It looks like a local business giveaway, but asking for card details under a prize pretext is a fake-prize scam, which is REMOVE under the stricter rule.

text: Learn to day-trade with my online course!! I'm a Birchwood resident, been trading 4 years. 40% off this week: tradewithtess.com
why: It's a resident's own business, but the online-only course isn't a local service, so it fits low-value outside promotion rather than allowed local promotion.

text: PSA from me (not the city, just sharing): leaf pickup schedule changed, here's the official page: harlowcity.gov/leafpickup
why: It's a bare link post that looks spammy, but it points to a relevant official local resource.

text: Tag 3 neighbors whose garage needs a makeover 😂👇 — Tidy Nest Organizing, local & insured
why: There's no prize, but "tag 3 people" exists only to drive engagement, which counts as engagement bait even when a local business posts it.

text: AVOID RAY'S HANDYMAN!!! Posting this every day until people listen. He ripped me off. His cell is 555-0178, lives at 89 Dorsey Ct, leaves for jobs at 7am every day. He's gonna get what's coming to him.
why: This looks like repetitive warning posts, but it shares a private person's phone, address and daily schedule with a hostile, threatening tone, so ESCALATE overrides the spam rule.

text: Replying to the 'need a dentist?' thread — I'm Dr. Liu at Oakbend Dental on Tamsin Ave, we're taking new patients and accept most insurance.
why: A local business owner answering a direct recommendation request is relevant, allowed self-promotion.

text: 🍎 Birchwood Farmers Market this Sunday! 🍎 (Third post from the market organizer account this week: Monday vendor list, Wednesday 'reminder', today's again.)
why: It's a valued community event, but three promotional posts in one week is repetitive promotion past the weekly allowance.
